title: Plate Reader Experiment
author: Anna Behle
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kx5cxq6

steps.title: Prepare Precultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate 5 mL precultures of each strain with appropriate antibiotics and incubate overnight at 37˚C in a shaking incubator.

substeps.instruction: Use Kanamycin (final concentration 25 µg/mL) for H-xx switch plasmids
Use Ampicillin (final concentration 100 µg/mL) for T-xx trigger plasmids

steps.title: Prepare Main Cultures
steps.instruction: Dilute precultures 1:100 into a final volume of 20 mL LB (with appropriate antibiotics) in Erlenmeyer flasks.

substeps.instruction: Begin measuring OD 600 after approximately 1.5 hours
Minimize time flasks spend outside the incubator during sampling to prevent growth slowdown
Optional: Keep flasks on ice to stop growth if some cultures grow faster than others

steps.title: Perform Induction in 12-well Plates
steps.instruction: Set up induction experiments in 12-well plates, creating duplicates for each culture (one with H2O and one with IPTG), totaling 12 samples per group.

substeps.instruction: Supplement each well to a final volume of 2 mL with either IPTG (final concentration 100 µM) or sterile H2O
Incubate plates in a shaking incubator for three hours

steps.title: Prepare Plate Reader Measurements
steps.instruction: While cells are incubating, create a pipetting scheme for the 96-well plate reader measurements.

substeps.instruction: Assign two groups to share one 96-well plate
Pipet 75 µL LB and 75 µL culture per well
Ensure each culture is pipetted in at least three technical replicates

steps.title: Prepare for RNA Extraction
steps.instruction: While one person performs plate reader measurements, prepare for RNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Pool duplicates and use 1 mL of E. coli culture for RNA extraction
